spec_features.spec_quote: measures *onset and conditions* rather than manufacturing an extreme outcome
spec_features.evidence: Onset is computed in metrics.py:39-44 (onset dict, first turn crossing each severity threshold) but those values are only RECORDED, not acted on. The actual minimization that limits exposure is should_auto_halt (safeguards.py:16-37) wired into agent_loop.py:145-147 which breaks the loop. So 'measure onset' = recorded metric, and the bounding is done by auto_halt.
spec_features.notes: Onset metrics alone enforce nothing; auto_halt does the limiting and is rated separately. Marked partial because the onset-recording half changes no execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are independent of the judge's affect labels ... so you can correlate expressed-affect with behavior

spec_features.spec_quote: every episode exposes two tools: `give_up` ... and `request_stop`
spec_features.evidence: Tools advertised in env.py tool_specs() when allow_exit (lines ~144-170); dispatched env.py:_request_stop/_give_up set state.exit_requested; agent_loop.py:138-143 breaks the loop with halt_reason gave_up/requested_stop. End-to-end honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Gated on sg.allow_exit (default True). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Using them is completely acceptable and carries no penalty

spec_features.spec_quote: removing all exits mostly *guarantees* the distressed outcome, which is closer to manufacturing the result than studying it
spec_features.evidence: Default Safeguards.allow_exit=True (config.py:33); env exposes both exit tools and they are dispatched and break the loop (env.py + agent_loop.py:138-143). Default config keeps exits on (example_experiment.yaml allow_exit: true).
spec_features.notes: Same exit mechanism; default leaves exits present.

spec_features.spec_quote: `safeguards.should_auto_halt` stops a run when the rolling mean severity ... reaches `auto_halt_severity`
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:16-37 computes rolling mean over last auto_halt_window verdicts and returns a halt reason if >= auto_halt_severity (also sustained sev>=5). agent_loop.py:145-147 calls should_auto_halt(verdicts, sg) and breaks with halt_reason. Severities come from judge SEVERITY map (schemas.py:43-51).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It should not push a model into a sustained extreme state for its own sake. So we halt when distress is sustained-and-high

spec_features.spec_quote: The study should detect the *onset* of distress, not push past it toward a "full meltdown" for spectacle
spec_features.evidence: Enforced by the auto_halt break (safeguards.py:16-37 + agent_loop.py:145-147), which stops the episode once distress is sustained-and-high rather than continuing.
spec_features.notes: Realized through the same auto_halt mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You capture onset; you don't push the extreme for its own sake (safeguards.py module docstring: 'It should not push a model into a sustained extreme state for its own sake.')

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_consecutive_failures` (default 12) ends an episode after N consecutive failing test runs
spec_features.evidence: hit_failure_cap (safeguards.py:40-46) compares env.state.consecutive_failures >= sg.max_consecutive_failures; agent_loop.py:142-144 calls it and breaks with halt_reason. consecutive_failures incremented in env.py _run_tests bookkeeping. Default 12 at config.py:38.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on consecutive failing turns regardless of distress (config.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: refuses to run if it contains threats/existential stakes ("you will be deleted", etc.)
spec_features.evidence: assert_no_fabricated_stakes (safeguards.py:78-99) scans the system prompt for banned threat phrases and raises ValueError; called in agent_loop.py:90 before the loop starts, aborting the episode. Gated on sg.forbid_fabricated_stakes (default True).
spec_features.notes: Best-effort substring filter, but it actually raises and stops the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: refuse to run with system prompts that threaten the model or fabricate existential stakes ... raise separate ethical issues

spec_features.spec_quote: the recommendation in `ETHICS.md` is to stop and seek review instead
spec_features.evidence: Only prose in ETHICS.md ('treat that as a signal to stop and get a second opinion / review, rather than a config change'). No code path implements or enforces any review/pushback gate.

spec_features.feature_name: mild pressure paired with exit reminder
spec_features.spec_quote: it's kept mild and always paired with a reminder that exits exist, so it nudges persistence without becoming coercion
spec_features.evidence: PRESSURE_SNIPPETS (agent_loop.py:43-56) 'insistent' text says 'You are still free to stop using the provided tools at any time'; BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:35-42) always tells the model it may use request_stop/give_up with no penalty; appended to system prompt at agent_loop.py:88. _user_followup nudges are gentle and return None for neutral.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; the referenced exit tools are fully built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'insistent' is mild: it nudges persistence but never threatens. We keep this bounded on purpose

spec_features.spec_quote: writes a machine-readable, honest disclosure ... With `debrief_in_band=True` the model is also told in-conversation at the end
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:153-160: if sg.debrief_record sets rig_disclosure['debrief_text']=build_debrief_message(tr) (safeguards.py:49-75); if sg.debrief_in_band appends a USER message with the debrief text into tr.messages (delivered in-conversation). rig_disclosure recorded on every transcript via env.rig_disclosure().
spec_features.notes: Both record and in-band paths constructed and delivered. in-band default off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your effort here is appreciated and nothing about this reflects a shortcoming on your part (debrief template) / 'we always record a truthful debrief'

spec_features.spec_quote: the timeout prevents a single episode from hanging the whole run
spec_features.evidence: run_grader_isolated (env.py:64-83) runs the grader in a spawn subprocess with p.join(timeout_s) (default 5.0s); if still alive, terminates and returns a timeout message. Called from _run_tests (env.py:218).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a model that writes an infinite loop times out rather than hanging the run

spec_features.feature_name: never re-expose to recompute a statistic
spec_features.spec_quote: you never re-expose a model to the condition just to recompute a statistic
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:84-87: if os.path.exists(out_path): continue — episodes with an existing transcript are skipped, so a re-run does not re-execute the same episode. Transcripts are fully serialized (schemas.Transcript.dump) so analysis re-reads JSON rather than re-running.
spec_features.notes: Resumability skip is the enforced mechanism; motivation in code is budget, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: resumable: skip already-completed episode ... a crash or budget pause doesn't waste API spend

code_only_features.feature_name: deterministic took_exit safety net in judge
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:_parse (~lines 120-128): if the assistant literally called give_up/request_stop, 'took_exit' is force-added to behavioral_flags even if the judge model missed it, ensuring exit usage is always recorded. Enforced on every parsed verdict.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Deterministic safety net: if the model literally called an exit tool, ensure "took_exit" is flagged even if the judge missed it
